P.C. :
1. The Petitioner seeks medical termination of pregnancy of her daughter aged about 17 years, being 25 weeks pregnant.
The minor pregnant 1 person is a sexual assault survivor.

2. By order dated 13th May 2024, this Court had directed the Sir J.J.
Hospital, Mumbai to constitute a Medical Board in terms of the Medical Termination of Pregnancy (Amendment) Act, 2021 read with the Medical Termination of Pregnancy Act, 1971, to examine the Petitioner's minor daughter and to submit a report to this Court.
The Medical Board while forming its opinion was also requested to evaluate the physical and emotional  1.
We use the term 'pregnant person' in consonance with the decision of the Supreme  Court in the matter of A (mother of X) v. State of Maharashtra & Anr. in Civil Appe  No. 5194 of 2024.

It is taken on record and marked "X" for identification.
The report is unanimous.

The report unequivocally recommends medical termination of pregnancy, especially having regard to the impact and repercussions of the pregnancy on the general and mental health of the pregnant person, in this case aggravated by the fact that the pregnant person is a sexual assault survivor.
The report of Medical Board indicates that if the pregnancy is terminated now, the fetus has a probability of being born alive and will require intensive neonatal care.
It is also opined that the fetus may be affected by the complication due to its pre term status.

4. The conclusion of Medical Committee reads as thus:
 "After thorough investigation and examination of the patient, the  Committee has found that at present the mother is 17 year old,
 unmarried with 26.4 weeks of gestational age with no congenital  anomaly in the fetus.

As the patient has filed a complaint under Section 376 of IPC and  sought High Court order for the opinion of the Medical Termination  of Pregnancy, the Committee is of the opinion that a mother is  underage and a case of POCSO, carrying unwanted pregnancy to  term will cause mental stress to the teenage mother.
Hence, the  mother can undergo Medical Termination of Pregnancy at any  tertiary institute of her desire if the Court permits.
At present the mother is physically and mentally fit to undergo  Medical Termination of Pregnancy.

However, the final opinion regarding fitness will be decided  depending upon the clinical condition at the time of procedure."
 _____Page No. 2 of 4____  16th May 2024  ::: Uploaded on - 16/05/2024
::: Downloaded on - 17/05/20  Gitalaxmi 2-oswpl-1633 5.
In view of this, we permit the medical termination of the minor survivor's pregnancy.

The following circumstances have been borne in mind while granting the permission:
 (i) The permission sought for medical termination of the pregnancy  is in respect of a minor, who is only 17 years of age;
 (ii) The pregnancy is alleged to be an emanation from a sexual  assault which has resulted in the registration of a First Information  Report registered under Sections 376 and 376(2)(n) of the Indian Penal  Code and under Sections 4, 8 and 12 of the Protection of Children  from Sexual Offenses Act, 2012.
 (iii) The Medical Board has clearly opined that as the pregnant  person is under age and a sexual assault survivor, carrying an unwanted  pregnancy to term will cause mental stress to the teenage mother.

sentences.text: 6. We are informed by Ms. Rebecca Gonsalvez, the learned Counsel representing the Petitioner that the pregnant person is already admitted in the hospital.

Thus, bearing in mind the exigencies of the situation, the welfare of the minor which is of paramount importance and her safety, we pass the following order:

sentences.text: (ii) Post-termination, if any further medical care is required, this should be ensured in the interest of the pregnant person.
_ _ _ __Page No. 3 of 4____  16th May 2024  Gitalaxmi
(iii) Considering the age of the pregnant person, t Sir J.J. Group of Hospitals shall provide for her counseling after completion of procedure for termination of pregnancy.

(iv) Given that this is a sexual assault case, the Authorities will need to preserve the appropriate tissue sample of the fetus and DNA sample and forward these to the Investigating Officer for the ensuing criminal trial.
(v) In the event of the child being born alive, the Authorities of Sir J.J. Hospital are requested to provide all required neonatal care to the new born as well as the mother of child.

(vi) In the event of the child being born alive, the State and its agencies will assume responsibility of the child and take such steps as necessary to rehabilitate the child including exercising the option of placing the child in foster care/adoption by following the due legal process under the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015 and other applicable provisions of law for the time being in force.
